summary.text: Orlando Ramos is a Democratic state representative from Massachusetts who has represented the 9th Hampden District since January 2021 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
A Springfield native, he previously served as the city's license commissioner.

paragraphs.text: Ramos was born and lives in Springfield, Massachusetts, and he graduated from Putnam Vocational Technical High School in 2000.

He earned an associate degree from Springfield Technical Community College, a bachelor's degree in public policy from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and a master of public administration from Westfield State University.
His career experience includes an internship in the office of former Governor Deval Patrick and service as license commissioner for the City of Springfield.
Ramos assumed office on January 6, 2021, succeeding Jose Tosado.

For the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Committees on Advanced Information Technology, the Internet, and Cybersecurity, on Transportation, and on Ways and Means, and he is vice chair of the Joint Committee on Racial Equity, Civil Rights, and Inclusion.
